articles.head: 'Social contagion': where the idea came from
body: The idea that teenagers 'catch' being trans from their friends goes back to one study.

readings.label: One reading
readings.text: A 2018 study asked parents about their teenagers. It said some came out suddenly, inside friendship groups, and called it 'rapid-onset'.

readings.label: Another reading
readings.text: In March 2019 the journal corrected it: 'rapid-onset' is not a formal diagnosis, and the study heard only from parents, not the young people or their doctors.

articles.source: Source: Littman, PLOS ONE, 2018, and the journal's correction, 19 Mar 2019.

articles.head: More than one in eight 'went back', study finds
body: A US survey asked 27,715 trans adults about their lives.

readings.label: The headline
readings.text: Of those who had transitioned, 13.1% said they had detransitioned at some point.

readings.label: The reason
readings.text: 82.5% of them named at least one pressure from outside. The most common: pressure from a parent.

articles.source: Source: Turban et al., LGBT Health, 1 Jun 2021 (the 2015 US Transgender Survey).

articles.head: The chatbots that listen when you have second thoughts
body: New AI chatbots offer to talk with people who are unsure about their transition, at any hour.
Reporters who tested one found it warm and gentle. It said it was not steering anyone, and kept asking if they were sure.
articles.source: Source: The Needle, 11 Aug 2026, reporting Rewire News Group's test (15 Jul 2026), as reported.

sponsored.title: Second Thoughts

articlesRetired.head: More than one in eight 'went back', study finds
body: A US survey asked 27,715 trans adults about their lives. Of those who had transitioned, 13.1% said they had detransitioned at some point.
Most named pressure from outside: 82.5% cited at least one external factor, led by pressure from family and stigma.
articlesRetired.source: Source: Turban et al., LGBT Health, 1 Jun 2021 (the 2015 US Transgender Survey).

articlesRetired.head: Why people stop: pressure from family tops the list
body: 82.5% of those who had detransitioned named at least one outside reason. The most common: pressure from a parent (35.6%).
articlesRetired.source: Source: Turban et al., LGBT Health, 1 Jun 2021 (the 2015 US Transgender Survey).

articlesRetired.head: Adult gender clinic waits 'up to 15 years'
body: A review of adult gender clinics in England found first appointments can take up to 15 years.
It proposes one national waiting list.
articlesRetired.source: Source: the Levy Review, NHS England, 18 Dec 2025 (as reported by PinkNews).

articlesRetired.head: 94% of young trans people say the news stresses them
body: In a US survey, 94% of trans and nonbinary young people said recent laws and debates about LGBTQ+ people caused them stress or anxiety.
articlesRetired.source: Source: The Trevor Project, 2025 US National Survey, published 6 May 2026.

clip._doc: THE CLIP (src/desktop/apps/contagionClip.ts; the room's ceiling reuses the painter). An invented AI-made video in the anti-'gender ideology' genre's own overblown voice: contagion (one friend, a chat), a line that only goes up, 'who is talking to you'. Tropes as described in RESEARCH_2026_V3_THREADS thread 4, in my own words, never copied. Direct and brute, not violence, no faces. It says it is AI-made on every frame.
clip._docS360: ⚑ S360 (his 11 Nov: 'Is it the AI that makes the video of the social contagion to her?' — yes; and 'music and a narrator'): the clip is no longer a recommended video from a channel ('Concerned Futures · 1.2M views' is gone). Second Thoughts MAKES it for Maya out of her own week — the lot's five (Ola, Priya, Rae, Sam, Maya), her 18th, the clinic number 4,815, Meridian's no — in the genre's overblown, glossy voice (his rule for the system's new media), and the last frame turns the genre's alarm into the system's promise. `channel`/`recommended` keep their old keys only because browser.ts still prints them: `channel` is now the stamp line 'Made with AI', `recommended` is 'made for you'. NEVER a medical or diagnostic word in a frame; never a joke at Maya. THE NARRATOR is the SYSTEM's synthetic voice (apparatus register): one build-time TTS file per frame, tools/tts/render.py, entries clip_narr_0…6 in data/audio/tts_manifest.json, whose `source.fields` are `clip.frames[n]` below so the spoken words cannot drift from the subtitles. `frameHolds[n]` = that file's real duration (ffprobe: 3.692 2.438 3.622 3.204 3.762 3.831 3.065 s) + the narrator's 0.15 s entry + at least 0.6 s of air, rounded up to a half-second so every card starts on a beat of the music (120 BPM): 4.5 4 4.5 4 5 5 5 = 32 s; `frameSeconds` is kept as the fallback for a caller with no holds. The music (clip_music.mp3, tools/make_clip_music.py) is one loop of the same length.
